articles.title: US Open tennis 2026: Shelton v Hurkacz, Choinski v Van de Zandschulp, and more on day four – live
articles.summary: Tennis updates from Flushing Meadows, New York. Email Katy and follow us on TikTok and Bluesky. And Nakashima breaks too – he’s hitting it hard off both wings and I wonder if he’s in the process of finding a new level.
body: Alex de Minaur said he was “broken inside” after his fourth-round exit at Wimbledon, and he was similarly deflated after the French Open, but his first slam as a married man (after his wedding to Katie Boulter) seems to be lifting his spirits, because the sixth seed has sprinted through the opening set against Italy’s Andrea Guerrieri, taking it 6-2, and he already has a break at 3-2 in the second. It’s one of the first-round matches that didn’t get on yesterday.

But Fearnley just can’t buy a hold, and he drops serve again. So Etcheverry leads 6-3, 3-1, while Choinski is pulled back to 5-5 in the tie-break … VDZ is two points from victory, make that one because it’s quickly 6-5. The match point is, at least, on Choinski’s serve, but the Brit bashes a forehand long and this rain-delayed opening-round match is over. The good news for British fans: Fran Jones and Toby Samuel will follow on Court 5.

articles.title: Lando Norris launches LN4 Fusion team to develop young drivers in F1 and motorsport
articles.summary: F1 champion first to back junior team in single-seater era. Norris also creates legacy programme to support talent. Lando Norris has co-founded a new junior, single-seater racing team.
body: Norris’s involvement, including a personal financial undertaking alongside an investment group, represents the first time an F1 world champion has directly backed a team in the modern junior single-seater era. As part of the project he has also established the LN4 Legacy programme, a driver development initiative designed to identify and support talent coming through the ranks from karting upwards and then provide assistance financially as well as in coaching, performance and career support.

The McLaren driver launched the project at an event in Monza, which will host the Italian Grand Prix this weekend. It constitutes a serious and comprehensive effort to address some of the difficulties facing junior drivers coming through the ranks, which Norris has previously identified as a fundamental problem for the sport.
“I know that getting to Formula One takes so much more than just talent. You need the right people around you, the right support and the right opportunities at the right time,” he said.

articles.title: Northern Ireland boss O'Neill 'hopeful' training centre plans progress
articles.summary: Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill says that he is "certainly hopeful" that the Irish Football Association can move forward with plans to have a National Training Centre open by 2028.
body: The IFA announced in February 2025 their plans for the "state-of-the-art" facility which will be located next to the Galgorm Resort just outside of Ballymena and will have "world-class pitches and cutting-edge training facilities".
The association reiterated their desire to proceed with the proposal last month, but did say they hope to "mitigate concerns where possible" after objections from local residents.
O'Neill, who grew up in Ballymena, believes having the facility at Galgorm will have a positive impact on the town.

"It's important that you do have a national training centre that kids are used to coming to from a young age. It's an elite facility that shows the intent from the association as they continue to develop players," he told BBC Sport NI's Stephen Watson.

articles.title: England drop fast bowler Brydon Carse for third Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston
articles.summary: Carse also missed second Test after incident in Derby bar. Matthew Fisher absence is only change from Lord’s squad. Brydon Carse has been left out of England’s squad for the final Test of the summer, against Pakistan at Edgbaston next week, with police still investigating allegations of an assault…
body: As a result of the allegations, and with investigations ongoing, Carse was dropped from the squad for last week’s second Test. The 31-year-old had been in the squad for the first game, but not named in the XI. Sonny Baker, who replaced him for the second Test but also did not play, remains in a squad that has changed only by the absence of Matthew Fisher. Alongside Baker, the other squad members who were not in the team at Lord’s are Shoaib Bashir, Sam Cook and Ollie Pope.

After England sealed the series win with victory at Lord’s Marcus Trescothick, the interim coach, promised that “we’re not going to ease off the gas” and spoke of the benefit the side’s current first-choice seamers – Jofra Archer, Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson – would get from regularly playing together. “The more experience everyone gets together, then it sort of fits into place how you want it to be.”

articles.title: US cyclist Ezra Caudell hospitalized with ‘multi-system trauma’ after Philadelphia crash
articles.summary: 19-year-old remains hospitalized after Sunday crash. Caudell receiving care for ‘multi-system trauma’ Lotto-Intermarché yet to update on Milan Menten. American cyclist Ezra Caudell remains hospitalized with “multi-system trauma” after being seriously injured in a crash during Sunday’s Philadelphia…
body: The 19-year-old Modern Adventure Pro Cycling rider was involved in a collision with Belgium’s Milan Menten of Lotto-Intermarché early in the men’s race. Caudell was knocked unconscious in the crash and both riders were taken to local hospitals for treatment, according to the Philadelphia Inquirer.
Modern Adventure posted an update on Caudell’s condition to social media on Tuesday evening, two days after the accident.
“Ezra remains hospitalized and is actively receiving care for multi-system trauma he sustained as a result of his crash at the Philadelphia Cycling Classic,” the team said.
“He has an incredible team working diligently and family at his bedside. We are grateful for the thoughts and ongoing outpouring of support.”

articles.title: Anderson in wickets but Middlesex recover against Lancs
articles.summary: James Anderson takes two early wickets on his return for Lancashire but Middlesex recover on a rain-affected day one in the County Championship.
body: Luke Hollman rained on Sir James Anderson's parade as Middlesex reached 139-3 on a murky, rain-reduced opening day of the Division Two clash between Middlesex and Lancashire at Merchant Taylors' School.
Anderson returned from a two-month absence with a calf problem to lead a Red Rose County attempting to avoid one of the worst County Championship finishes in its history.
Displaying all the craft of his 44 years, Anderson took two early wickets on route to 2-30 on a day where only 39 overs were bowled due to rain and bad light.

However, Hollman, pressed into service as an opener for the second match in succession, passed 50 for the 10th time in his first-class career, finishing on 54 not out to lead Middlesex to calmer waters before the weather closed in.

articles.title: Rain severely affects opening day of Notts v Leics
articles.summary: Nottinghamshire captain Haseeb Hameed passes 9,000 first-class career runs on a rain-disrupted first day against relegation-threatened Leicestershire.
body: The County Championship defending champions and Division One leaders made what they could of the 10.3 overs that were possible at Trent Bridge to reach 42-0.
Hameed is unbeaten on 32, having hit six boundaries in difficult conditions under a leaden sky after his counterpart Ian Holland won the toss and opted to bowl first on a green-tinged surface.

Play could not begin in earnest until almost six hours after the 10:30 BST September start time and although the rain did not return, it was not long before bad light became an issue and umpires James Middlebrook and Neil Pratt decided it was too dark to continue.
Earlier, after rain had washed out the opening session, the players had been able to make a 13:30 BST start only to be forced off again after a single over.

articles.title: Bengals QB Joe Burrow's goals? 'I just want to win this year'
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow was the first guest on teammate Ja'Marr Chase 's new podcast, "Chasing No 1" with co-host Annie Agar. Chase asked during the podcast about Burrow's objectives for the upcoming season. "Do you go into the season with goals?" Chase asked Burrow.
body: "I just want to win this year," Burrow said. "I just want to win. The rest will take care of itself. We'll break a bunch of records eventually, but I think we're going to have a really good team that has a chance to win every game that we step foot on the field for. I don't know about you, but I could really feel it in my bones (and) in my soul in OTAs this year − different from years past.
Agar asked Burrow whether he listens to criticism from people or cares about it.
In an in-game interview with CBS sideline reporter AJ Ross during the Bengals' final preseason game in Philadelphia, Burrow said he tries to treat every day like it's his last.

articles.title: Fury launches fresh swipe at Joshua as talks continue
articles.summary: Tyson Fury has branded Anthony Joshua a "coward" and suggested the two-time world heavyweight champion is "conning everybody" as talks over a long-awaited all-British showdown continue.
body: Fury and Joshua had appeared closer than ever to agreeing a super-fight long-in-the-making, only for Saudi organisers Sela's wish to hold the event in the USA to emerge as a major stumbling block.
Joshua's side have maintained their desire for the fight to take place in the UK.
Fury took to Instagram once again on Wednesday to question the hold up.

"Joshua, where are you? Still no deal done. It's getting quite tiring," said Fury. "I've been down to fight in every location that's been mentioned - England, Ireland, Vegas, New York, back to England, back to Ireland, back to New York. I've said yep, yep, yep every single time with zero stipulations.

articles.title: Hadjar to miss Italian GP with ongoing wrist injury
articles.summary: Isack Hadjar will miss this weekend's Italian Grand Prix due to his ongoing wrist injury, with Liam Lawson replacing him for a second consecutive event at Red Bull.
body: Hadjar suffered the injury while boxing in training during the summer break last month which forced him to miss the Dutch Grand Prix and he has not recovered in time for Monza.
With Lawson stepping up to be Max Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull, Yuki Tsunoda will have another chance to impress at Racing Bulls.

Red Bull only made the decision on Wednesday afternoon to give Hadjar every chance to drive but medical staff have decided he should miss another event and hope to return for the following race in Madrid next weekend.
"Liam will drive alongside Max at the Italian Grand Prix in Monza, while Isack continues to make encouraging progress following the wrist injury sustained during the summer break," said Red Bull.

articles.title: Cameron says talks are 'advanced' to fight Shields
articles.summary: Chantelle Cameron says that talks for her to fight Claressa Shields are advanced and moving quickly following her victory over Mikaela Mayer.
body: Cameron defeated Mayer by unanimous decision in a thriller to become WBA, WBC and WBO super-welterweight world champion at MPW-06 in Birmingham on Saturday.

She emerged victorious, edging a tight contest 97-93, 97-93, 96-94 on the judges' scorecards, further glossing a stellar resume that already honours her as the only woman to ever defeat the great Katie Taylor in her professional career.
With the victory strengthening Cameron's claim to a place among the greats of the women's game, she now has eyes on taking on the self-proclaimed 'GWOAT' [Greatest woman of all time] in Shields.

Many thought a rematch with Mayer would be next on her list, but Cameron told Sky Sports that things are moving rapidly with the WBC and WBA middleweight champion, who has a record of 19-0 across multiple weight divisions.
